Hydra Facial in Jaipur | Cleanse, Exfoliate & Hydrate

A hydra facial, also called hydradermabrasion, is a multi-step facial that cleanses and exfoliates the skin, lifts debris out of blocked pores with gentle suction and then applies hydrating serums, usually with no downtime. At Kezza, hydra facials are done in a clinical setting at our Jaipur and Sikar clinics, with each step adjusted to your skin.

The Treatment

What Is a Hydra Facial?

Hydradermabrasion combines gentle exfoliation with water-based suction. A handpiece with a spiral tip glides over the skin, loosening dead cells and surface debris while drawing them away, and at the same time releases a cleansing or hydrating solution onto the skin. Unlike older crystal microdermabrasion, nothing gritty is blasted onto the face.

A typical session moves through four stages: cleansing and exfoliation, a mild acid peel to soften what is inside the pores, extraction with suction, and infusion of serums with ingredients such as hyaluronic acid and antioxidants. Depending on the machine and your skin, further steps can be added or left out.

It is best thought of as a deep-cleaning and hydrating facial rather than a treatment for skin disease. Research on hydradermabrasion is limited to small studies, so it is used to keep skin clear, smooth and comfortable, alongside medical treatment when a condition such as acne or pigmentation needs it.

In Short:

  • Four steps: cleanse, peel, extract and hydrate.
  • Little downtime: most people go straight back to their day.
  • Maintenance: works best repeated every few weeks.
Benefits

What a Hydra Facial Can Help With

Blocked Pores

Suction extraction lifts blackheads and oil from congested pores, especially on the nose and chin.

Dull, Dry Skin

Exfoliation and hydrating serums leave the skin feeling smoother and looking fresher straight after.

Oily Skin

Regular deep cleansing helps manage shine and congestion between other treatments.

Little or No Downtime

Most people return to work or go out the same day; any mild redness usually fades within hours.

Before an Event

A popular refresher before weddings and functions, ideally a few days ahead rather than on the day.

With Medical Care

Can be combined with acne or pigmentation treatment when your doctor advises it.

Suitability

Is a Hydra Facial Right for You?

Hydra facials suit most skin types, but they are a maintenance treatment, not a cure for skin conditions.

A hydra facial may suit you if

  • You have congested pores, blackheads or oily skin
  • Your skin looks dull or feels dry and rough
  • You want a refreshing facial without peeling or downtime
  • You are having medical skin treatment and want gentle upkeep between sessions

Wait, or check with your doctor first, if

  • You have an active rash, sunburn, a cold sore or broken skin on the face
  • You have a rosacea flare or very reactive skin
  • You are pregnant; ask your doctor before any aesthetic treatment
  • You use isotretinoin or strong retinoids, or have had a peel or laser treatment recently
  • You are allergic to aspirin (salicylates) or have reacted to acid peels before

A hydra facial will not remove acne scars, melasma or deep lines. For those, ask about acne scar treatment or pigmentation treatment.

Procedure

What Happens During a Hydra Facial

A session takes about an hour, including a quick skin check.

01

Skin Check

The therapist or doctor checks your skin type, any sensitivity and the products you use, and adjusts the steps and solutions.

02

Cleanse & Exfoliate

The spiral tip removes surface oil and dead skin while a cleansing solution is released.

03

Mild Peel

A gentle acid solution loosens debris inside the pores; the strength is lowered for sensitive skin.

04

Extraction

Suction lifts blackheads and debris out of the pores; it feels like a light pulling on the skin.

05

Hydrate & Protect

Hydrating serums are applied, followed by moisturiser and sunscreen.

Timeline

Hydra Facial Results and Timing

The effect is immediate but temporary, so it is usually repeated.

D1

Straight After

Skin looks fresher and feels smoother; slight pinkness usually fades within a few hours.

D2

Next 24 to 48 Hours

Skip scrubs, peels, waxing and heavy makeup, and protect your skin from the sun.

W1

First Week

Pores look clearer; oily skin may feel less congested.

W4

Every 2 to 4 Weeks

Repeating the facial keeps pores clear, as advised for your skin.

M3

Longer Term

Results last longest with daily sunscreen and a routine that suits your skin.

Medical Note: Results vary from person to person. This page is general information from Kezza Hair & Skin Clinic and is not a substitute for a consultation with a doctor.

Hydra facials for different skin types

  • Oily and congested skin: the extraction step is the main benefit, clearing blackheads and excess oil. Regular sessions can help keep pores clear.
  • Dry and dull skin: exfoliation removes flaky surface cells and the serums add hydration, so the skin feels softer and looks brighter for a while.
  • Sensitive skin: the peel strength and suction can be lowered, and some steps can be skipped. Avoid a session during a flare of rosacea or eczema.
  • Acne-prone skin: useful for blackheads and whiteheads once inflamed acne is under medical control; it is not a replacement for treatment.

How it differs from a salon facial and a chemical peel

A standard salon facial cleanses and massages the skin, often with manual extraction that can leave marks if done roughly. A hydra facial uses a machine to exfoliate and extract with controlled suction, then applies serums in the same session. A medical chemical peel works differently again: a stronger acid is left on the skin to resurface it, which can treat pigmentation and some acne scars but may cause peeling and needs more downtime. Your doctor can advise which of these suits your skin, or how to combine them safely.

A note on names

You will see the treatment advertised as hydra facial, hydrafacial, HydraFacial or aqua facial. HydraFacial is a trademarked brand of hydradermabrasion system; the general technique is also available on other machines. What matters for your skin is a hygienic setup, single-use tips where needed, and steps that are adjusted to your skin by trained staff.

Aftercare

  • Use a gentle cleanser and moisturiser for the rest of the day.
  • Apply sunscreen and avoid direct sun for a day or two.
  • Skip scrubs, peels, retinoids, waxing and saunas for 24 to 48 hours.
  • Leave makeup off for a few hours if you can.

What affects the cost of a hydra facial?

The cost depends on the steps and serums included, any add-ons, and whether you book a single session or a course. Your therapist or doctor explains the options after checking your skin.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a hydra facial the same as a HydraFacial?
Hydra facial is the everyday name for hydradermabrasion. HydraFacial is also the brand name of one company's hydradermabrasion system, and similar treatments are offered on other machines. The steps are much the same: cleanse, exfoliate, extract and hydrate. Ask us which system is used for your treatment.
How often should I have a hydra facial?
Many people repeat it every two to four weeks, depending on their skin type and goals. Oily, congested skin may benefit from more regular sessions, while dry or sensitive skin may need them less often. We suggest a schedule after your first session.
Does a hydra facial hurt?
Most people find it comfortable. The suction feels like a light pulling, and the peel step can tingle briefly. Tell the therapist if anything feels too strong, because the suction and solutions can be adjusted.
Is a hydra facial good for acne?
It can help with blackheads, whiteheads and oily skin, but it does not treat the causes of acne. Active, inflamed acne needs a doctor's treatment first; our acne treatment page explains the options. A hydra facial can then be used for upkeep.
When should I have one before my wedding?
Plan your last session a few days to a week before the event, so any slight redness has settled and your skin has had time to recover. If you have never had one, try a session a few weeks earlier to see how your skin reacts.
What should I avoid after a hydra facial?
For a day or two, avoid scrubs, peels, retinoid creams, waxing, saunas and heavy makeup, and use sunscreen. Keep the skin moisturised and let it settle before starting any stronger treatment.
